title: Traffic Rehearsal Horizon: Split Composer with Safety Lanes & Cost Impact Preview
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Operators currently lack a quick, low-risk way to rehearse traffic splits and understand both safety constraints and cost trade-offs before applying a rollout. This causes slow, conservative rollouts and escalations during incidents.

Goal: Design a Split Composer UX that lets teams assemble staged traffic splits, visualize safety lanes (hard/soft constraints), run a dry-run rehearsal against historical traffic slices, and preview estimated cost delta and token budget impact for each stage. The composer should enable one-click rollback rehearsals and produce an exportable runbook.

Success criteria:
- PM/Eng acceptance: Composer flows map cleanly to rollout APIs and runtime policies.
- Usability: Engineers can configure a simple canary and run a rehearsal in under 3 minutes in user testing.
- Safety: Rehearsal surfaces conflicts with active guardrails and suggests mitigations.
- Cost visibility: Per-stage cost delta and cumulative spend estimate are shown with confidence bands.

Constraints and considerations:
- Must integrate with existing rollout scheduling and canary signals in the Console.
- Rehearsal uses sampled historical traffic (read-only) — design must make that explicit for compliance.
- Compute cost estimation uses existing Optimize heuristics — UX should surface uncertainty.

Deliverables:
- Figma prototype of composer canvas, safety lanes panel, and cost preview modal.
- Clickable rehearsal simulation with timeline scrubber.
- Microcopy for safety warnings, export runbook, and rollback confirmation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Design passes a walkthrough with Runtime and Product within the cycle.
- Prototype includes 3 sample templates: Canary 5%, Phased A/B 50/50 split, and Traffic Shadowing.
- Developer handoff includes tokenized JSON schema mapping composer to rollout API and draft telemetry events.
comments: 2026-03-01 Asha Kapoor: Initial ticket created after discovery with two platform customers. They emphasized the need to see cost delta per stage to avoid surprise bills.
2026-03-03 Liam O'Connor: Sketched early composer canvas. Decided to try a timeline-first layout (left) with stage cards (center) and an expanding safety lane panel (right).
2026-03-04 Marin Park (PM): Requested explicit 'dry-run' label in the toolbar and an audit note that rehearsals are read-only and do not affect live routing.

2026-03-06 Design review meeting: Engineering flagged that rehearsals need telemetry hooks for simulated requests count and estimated token consumption. Agreed to surface confidence band for cost estimates.
2026-03-08 Usability test (3 engineers): Participants understood stage-level rollback but were confused by 'soft' vs 'hard' safety lanes; updated microcopy and added inline examples.

2026-03-10 Engineering feedback: Backend can provide stage-level cost delta and a conservative upper-bound. Will return data as {"estimate": number, "upper_bound": number, "sample_size": number}. Need microcopy to explain upper-bound.

2026-03-11 Asha Kapoor: Updated Figma prototype to include 'Rehearsal Summary' modal with cost confidence band, safety conflicts list, and runbook export. Marking ticket ready for PM/Runtime sign-off.
2026-03-12 Liam O'Connor: Prepared developer handoff notes and JSON mapping in attachments. Set up follow-up ENG ticket for telemetry (ENG-901234).
notes: Prototype introduces a new visual affordance: 'safety lanes' that lock stage parameters when a hard constraint is active. We should evaluate accessibility contrast for the lane overlays and ensure keyboard-first interactions for stage reordering.
next_steps: 1) PM/Runtime sign-off (this week). 2) Coordinate with ENG on telemetry schema and rehearsal sampling window. 3) Run 5 moderated usability sessions with platform engineers. 4) Finalize handoff and open engineering tickets for implementation.
